grounding.states: Ontario Structured Psychotherapy Program gives adults free, publicly funded CBT for depression and anxiety-related concerns
grounding.from: The Ontario Structured Psychotherapy Program (OSP) gives adults free, publicly funded cognitive-behavioural therapy for depression and anxiety-related concerns.

grounding.states: No Ontario health card or primary care provider needed; self-referral accepted
grounding.from: No Ontario health card or primary care provider is needed, and self-referrals are accepted.

grounding.states: Not suitable for everyone; does not cover unstructured talk therapy
grounding.from: It is not suitable for everyone, such as people with complex needs or conditions it doesn't treat. One OSP site lists what it does not cover: DBT, crisis or housing support, substance use counselling, relationship or family counselling, and unstructured talk therapy.

value.answer: Good on you for reaching out. In Toronto, the free option is the Ontario Structured Psychotherapy Program, which gives adults free CBT for depression and anxiety-related concerns. Search for it and fill out the referral form. You don't need an Ontario health card or a family doctor, and you can refer yourself. It isn't right for everyone, and it doesn't cover unstructured talk therapy. If you'd rather pay a little, student-intern training clinics run around $50 a session, and Fika is $65 online only. The $45 Centre for Training in Psychotherapy fee is from an older listing, so check it. I couldn't confirm any of these are taking new clients right now. I also didn't find a crisis line for Toronto, so if things get urgent, go to the nearest emergency department.
